title: CI result bundle: provenance.json and the verdicts.tsv row contract
description: A bundle is the directory rm-bundle/ in one CI job's artifacts: provenance.json (this schema), verdicts.tsv (rows per $defs/verdict_row) and optional logs/. The job writes it; the service pulls it by job id, checks it against the CI API's own record of the job, scans it, and only then reads it (D5, D11). Nothing is ever pushed to the service. Owner: T0 runner (writer), CI fetch/verify (reader). A4, D2, D4, D5, D6, D7, D11, PR9.

run_nonce.description: D5: issued by the service when it triggers the run, passed in the RM_REQUEST pipeline variable, and stamped on every verdicts.tsv row.

request.description: D5: what the service asked for. Equal to the stored RM_REQUEST ($defs/rm_request) with its `schema` and `nonce` fields removed (the nonce is carried in run_nonce). Verify compares both against the RM_REQUEST variable the CI API reports for this pipeline.

configuration.description: A configuration id, or @registry for the registry job (F3).

canonical_urls.description: D2: pinned URL (as .gitmodules writes it) -> anonymous HTTPS URL of the component's canonical repo, only for pins whose canonical repo is NOT the one the URL names (copies, aliases). Every other pin's canonical repo is its own URL, with ssh rewritten to https. Lets the job check canonical-host reachability without registry access or any credential.

ci.description: D5, A4: the job as the job saw itself. The service trusts only the CI API's copy of these values; this copy must match it.

harness_sha.description: The CI project's commit (CI_COMMIT_SHA): the pinned grader.

captured.description: D4, D5: what the job actually read, taken AFTER the gates ran. T0 fetches each pin into an empty repo and never checks out a working tree, so: superproject_commit = `git rev-parse FETCH_HEAD^{commit}` of the superproject fetch; pins = the gitlinks the t0.pins.fetchable walk actually read (`git ls-tree <parent> -- <path>`). superproject_commit must equal request.commit or the bundle is rejected (verify check 5, a consistency check: D5's authority for T0 rests on verify checks 1 to 4 and 6, which compare the bundle with the CI API's own record). From Phase 2 (D4) a nested pin that differs from the walker's pin makes the run UNVERIFIED.

pins.description: One entry per gitlink the job read, with the commit it found; null = the pin's parent could not be fetched, so the gitlink was not read.

commit.description: null = not checked out (could not be fetched).

tools.description: D4: tool versions. Phase 2 adds EDA tools.

nanosoc_rm.description: Version of the T0 runner package.

host.description: D4, D7 (Phase 2): load at start and end, used to call a timeout INFRA rather than FAIL.

cpu_seconds.description: D10 (Phase 2): CPU time the job used, for budgeting in CPU-hours. Optional in v1.

ip_hash.description: D4 (Phase 2): sha256 over the IP files the file lists resolved.

scan.description: D11: the job's own vendor scan of rm-bundle/, run by finalise_bundle() as the job's last step, BEFORE artifact upload. Flagged or unscanned files are deleted from rm-bundle/ and only their locations are kept in `findings` (never the matched text). The service scans again and trusts only its own result.

rm_request.description: D5, A4: the RM_REQUEST pipeline variable, compact JSON, exactly as the service built, stored and sent it (interfaces.md section 10, Trigger step 1). Verify check 2 compares the CI API's copy byte for byte with the stored bytes.

verdict_row.description: One verdicts.tsv line, parsed. Wire format, one line per row, UTF-8, LF: <utc>\t<STATUS>\t<gate id>\t<detail>\t<nonce>. The first four fields are exactly what the toolkit's ci/lib.sh _ci_record writes and ci/collect-results.py read_verdicts parses (it ignores a fifth field). The fifth, the run nonce, is new. No header line. PR9, D5.

status.description: lib.sh's five (PASS, FAIL, UNVERIFIED, WARN, SKIP) plus INFRA (D7): an infrastructure failure, never counted as FAIL. A row G.negctl with PASS means gate G's negative control FIRED (G went red on its broken input); FAIL means it did not. The toolkit's collect-results.py maps neither INFRA nor WARN (its VERDICT_MAP gives them status None); this tool's roll-up (README section 6) handles both.

detail.description: Free text with no tab or newline. lib.sh's _ci_record does not strip them, so the runner replaces each tab or newline in a detail with one space before writing the row.

gate_verdict.description: The service's verdict for one gate after reading the rows and the control. WAIVED: the gate's raw verdict was FAIL or UNVERIFIED, its control fired, and every non-pass item is covered by a T0 waiver of a frozen configuration (README section 6). FLAKY, XFAIL and XPASS arrive in Phase 2 (D8).

gate_item.description: One line of rm-bundle/items/<gate>.jsonl: one item the gate judged (interfaces.md section 9, Output item 2). Configuration gates judge pins (`tree_path`); registry gates judge citations (`file` + `pointer`). `nanosoc-rm t0 items NONCE GATE` prints them from the stored bundle. T0 waivers match items by gate, `tree_path` and `result` (eligibility.schema.json `t0_waivers`, README section 6). `not-reached`: the item could not be judged because an item above it failed (a pin below an unfetched parent; a tree that was never fetched, so never scanned).
